patient_summary:
Hello there, you're here for a follow-up visit. We talked a lot about how you've been losing weight on a medicine called phentermine. Since your last visit, you've gained another pound. You've gained a pound the month before that too, and you haven't been able to lose any more weight than you had when you were at 136 pounds. You're feeling frustrated about this.

We agreed that if you keep gaining weight, you shouldn't keep taking phentermine. We don't want you to take it to keep your weight down, but only to help you lose weight. You agree with this.

Your doctor checked you and found everything is okay. You don't have any other problems. You look happy and don't seem upset. Your heart and lungs are okay too.

If you don't lose any more weight in the next month, we might have you stop taking phentermine. If you lose a few pounds, we'll keep you on it until you get close to your goal of 135 pounds. Then we'll try to keep you there for one or two months and then stop.

You agree with this plan. If you have any problems or feel worried, you can always talk to your doctor or nurse.
caregiver_checklist: Check her weight at home and record it.
Watch for shortness of breath, chest pain, or palpitations.
Call the doctor if she experiences any of these symptoms.
Schedule a follow-up appointment in one month.
Monitor her weight closely and record it weekly.
Watch for any signs of fatigue or dizziness.
Call the doctor if she experiences fatigue or dizziness.
Schedule a re-evaluation if she loses a couple of pounds.
Schedule a follow-up appointment if she does not lose weight in the next month.
Call the doctor if she gains more than a couple of pounds.
Schedule a re-evaluation if she reaches her goal of 135 pounds.
child_explanation: You've been trying to lose weight with a special medicine called phentermine. But you haven't been able to lose any more weight. You and the grown-ups are worried you might not need the medicine anymore. The doctors are taking good care of you. You look happy and healthy. They'll check again in a few days. If you don't lose any more weight, they'll stop the medicine. If you lose a little, they'll keep it for a while. You can talk to the doctors if you have any questions.
source_text: SUBJECTIVE:,  She is here for a followup on her weight loss on phentermine.  She has gained another pound since she was here last.  We talked at length about the continued plateau she has had with her weight.  She gained a pound the month before and really has not been able to get her weight any farther down than she had when her lowest level was 136.  She is frustrated with this as well.  We agree that if she continues to plateau she really should not stay on phentermine.  We would not want her to take it to maintain her weight but only to help her get her weight down, and she may have really lost any benefit from it, and she agrees.,REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:,  Otherwise negative.  She has no specific complaints.  No shortness of breath, chest pain or palpitations.,PHYSICAL EXAM:,Vital signs:  Her blood pressure is fine.  Her diastolic is a little bit high, but otherwise okay.,General:  She appears in good spirits.  No apparent distress.,HEENT:  Negative.,Neck:  Supple without bruits.,Chest:  Clear.,Cardiac exam:  Regular without extra sounds.,ASSESSMENT:,  Weight loss on phentermine, really has plateaued.,PLAN:,  If she does not lose weight in the next month we will probably consider having her go off the phentermine.  If she does lose a couple of pounds, then we will keep her on it until she gets closer to her goal of 135 and then try to keep her there for one or two months and then stop.  She agrees with this plan.
